plants.name: Hydrangea macrophylla
plants.description: Great rounded globes of tiny blossoms swell along the roadsides, temple paths and hillside gardens of Japan. Each head glows in shades that shift with the soil's chemistry. The flowers look especially dreamy against the soft grey skies and drizzle of the rainy season.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early June to early July, during Japan's rainy season (tsuyu)
plants.location: Japan, across most regions of the country
plants.funFact: Soil chemistry can change the colour of many hydrangeas. Acidic soil that makes aluminium available to the plant tends to give blue blooms, while more neutral to alkaline soil pushes them toward pink.

plants.name: Lavandula angustifolia
plants.description: Silvery, needle-leaved mounds send up slender spikes of violet-blue flowers. The blooms hum with bees and release a sweet, herbal fragrance on warm summer afternoons. It is a cottage-garden favourite and thrives in sunny borders and rock gardens.
plants.bloomingSeason: Early to mid-summer, so it is in flower around June 23 in the Northern Hemisphere
plants.location: Temperate gardens of the Northern Hemisphere, including Europe and North America (hardy in USDA zones 5–9)
plants.funFact: English lavender is among the hardiest lavenders. It copes with cold winters far better than many of its Mediterranean relatives, which is why it grows so widely in cooler climates.
